claims.statement: Bulbs frequently fail to rejoin the app or retain settings after a power interruption, indicating instability in state persistence.
Users report connection failures even when the light hub is in close proximity, suggesting issues with local network or protocol handshake.
Setup often fails to connect to WiFi, and retrofitting is sometimes required to enable smart functionality, pointing to onboarding friction.
Physical pole-base connections are reported as weak and prone to breakage under leverage, indicating hardware fragility.

mechanisms.statement: After a power cycle, bulbs lose stored network credentials or state due to volatile memory handling or missing persistent storage logic, causing them to become unresponsive until manually re-paired.
mechanisms.main_uncertainty: Whether firmware persists network credentials across power cycles is not confirmed by teardown or logs.

mechanisms.statement: WiFi setup fails due to inadequate handling of 2.4GHz-only requirements or captive portal interference, exacerbated by lack of clear user guidance during onboarding.
mechanisms.main_uncertainty: Specific network environment conditions (e.g., dual-band SSID merging) are not captured in reviews.

mechanisms.statement: Mechanical stress at the pole-base interface leads to physical disconnection or internal wire damage, especially during installation or adjustment.
mechanisms.main_uncertainty: Failure mode distribution between manufacturing defect vs. design flaw is unclear without failure analysis.

validation_tasks.task: Verify whether device firmware stores WiFi credentials and operational state in non-volatile memory across power cycles.
Test setup success rate across common home WiFi configurations (e.g., merged 2.4/5GHz SSIDs, enterprise auth, mesh networks).
Conduct mechanical stress testing on pole-base connection to determine failure threshold and root cause (material vs. geometry).

abstentions.reason: Observed evidence identifies symptoms but does not isolate whether reliability issues stem from firmware logic, cloud dependency, or hardware tolerances.
Compatibility failures with Alexa could arise from skill implementation, discovery payload errors, or runtime directive handling—reviews do not distinguish these layers.

actions.improvement_direction: Enable verification of state persistence across power cycles to resolve uncertainty about connectivity recovery failures.
actions.action: Implement firmware-level logging and telemetry for WiFi credential and operational state persistence during power-cycle events, and conduct controlled lab validation using the state persistence validation protocol.
actions.intervention_logic: This action directly addresses the uncertainty in M1 by generating evidence on whether credentials and settings are stored in non-volatile memory. It supports future corrective decisions without assuming the mechanism is true.
actions.validation_metric: ≥95% of test units retain WiFi credentials and prior settings after 10 consecutive power cycles under controlled conditions.

actions.improvement_direction: Improve robustness of WiFi setup logic to handle common home network configurations that currently cause onboarding failures.
actions.action: Enhance onboarding firmware to detect and adapt to merged 2.4/5GHz SSIDs, captive portals, and mesh network conditions, with fallback guidance for unsupported configurations.
actions.intervention_logic: M2 is assessed as plausible; this change conservatively hardens the setup process against known environmental variability without requiring hardware or third-party changes.
actions.validation_metric: Onboarding success rate increases from baseline to ≥90% across 15 representative home WiFi configurations, including dual-band merged SSIDs and mesh networks.

actions.improvement_direction: Reduce user-induced stress on fragile pole-base connections during installation through clearer handling instructions.
actions.action: Update in-app and printed installation guides to include explicit warnings against applying leverage at the pole-base joint and demonstrate safe handling techniques.
actions.intervention_logic: While M3 identifies a hardware fragility (supported), hardware changes are disallowed. This low-regret action mitigates exacerbating user behaviors and aligns with the supported mechanism’s scope.
actions.validation_metric: Post-update field reports show ≥20% reduction in 'broken connection during install' complaints within 3 months.

api_knowledge.functionality: The Alexa.ColorController interface enables users to control the color of lighting or other color-capable devices by voice commands. It defines a SetColor directive using the hue, saturation, and brightness (HSB) color model, supports state and change reporting, and integrates with Alexa discovery and endpoint health reporting.
api_knowledge.device_context: Applies to color-changing devices such as smart light bulbs or lighting fixtures that can represent colors in the hue, saturation, brightness (HSB) format and support Alexa Smart Home integration.

dependencies.trigger_condition: used to describe endpoints that support Alexa.ColorController during device discovery
required when reporting the health or connectivity status of the device to Alexa
often included in Discover.Response with Alexa.ColorController to report power state of the device
used for general error handling if a SetColor directive cannot be handled successfully
used for lighting endpoints to report colorTemperatureInKelvin when endpoint is set to a shade of white instead of a color
used to respond with generic Alexa.Response events after successfully handling SetColor directives

design_constraints: Colors must be represented using the hue, saturation, brightness (HSB) model.
The color property is required in the SetColor directive payload.
For best experience, maintain existing brightness when setting a new color.
Discovery responses must include retrievable and proactivelyReported flags for the color property.
Responses must include timeOfSample and uncertaintyInMilliseconds for each property.
common_root_causes: Skill fails to respond to SetColor directive with Alexa.Response or Alexa.ErrorResponse.
Brightness incorrectly overwritten instead of maintaining prior brightness value.
Retrievable or proactivelyReported flags not properly configured in discovery response.
Missing or malformed color property in context object during state report.
Invalid HSB color values outside supported numeric range.
api_knowledge.notes_for_root_cause_mapping: If a SetColor directive cannot be processed, the skill must return an Alexa.ErrorResponse event. When handling color changes, maintain the device's existing brightness level to ensure consistent user experience. Ensure retrievable and proactivelyReported properties are correctly declared in discovery; missing configuration may prevent state synchronization.

api_knowledge.functionality: Enables Alexa skills to control and report the color temperature of tunable white light devices, allowing users to adjust lighting warmth or coolness through voice commands or automation.
api_knowledge.device_context: Applies to tunable white lighting devices, such as smart bulbs or light fixtures, that support control of color temperature between 1,000 and 10,000 Kelvin.

dependencies.trigger_condition: used to describe endpoints that support Alexa.ColorTemperatureController during device discovery
required when reporting the health or connectivity status of the device to Alexa
often included in Discover.Response with Alexa.ColorTemperatureController to report power state of the device
used for error handling if a color temperature directive cannot be handled successfully or is not supported in the current device mode
for lighting endpoints that support both ColorController and ColorTemperatureController, report color state when endpoint is set to a color and colorTemperatureInKelvin when set to a shade of white
used to respond with generic Alexa.Response events after handling SetColorTemperature, IncreaseColorTemperature, or DecreaseColorTemperature directives

design_constraints: If the requested color temperature is unsupported, the device must set to the nearest valid value.
State reporting must include all retrievable properties in context.
Change reports must distinguish between color and color temperature states for devices that support both interfaces.
common_root_causes: Device in unsupported mode (e.g., HSB color mode) when color temperature control is requested.
Device unable to reach requested color temperature; must set to nearest possible value.
Missing or incorrect proactivelyReported/retrievable settings in discovery response.
api_knowledge.notes_for_root_cause_mapping: If the device is in a mode that does not support color temperature adjustment (for example, HSB color mode), Alexa responds with 'That only works when your light is set to a shade of white.'

api_knowledge.functionality: Enables devices to be turned on or off by Alexa and to report their current power state.
api_knowledge.device_context: Smart home devices that can be powered on or off, such as lights, vacuums, or appliances; can include connected vehicles with Alexa user identification.

dependencies.trigger_condition: used to describe endpoints that support Alexa.PowerController and define retrievable and proactively reported properties during device discovery
used to report the device's connectivity and operational health to Alexa, ensuring Alexa can display device health status
used together when a device supports both on/off and brightness adjustment, such as smart lights

design_constraints: powerState values must be ON or OFF
All properties must be retrievable in StateReport and proactivelyReported in ChangeReport
Device must respond to user requests in less than 2 seconds; over 5 seconds is a latency failure

common_root_causes: Property value not retrievable or not proactivelyReported
User verification required but not completed
api_knowledge.notes_for_root_cause_mapping: If a TurnOn or TurnOff directive cannot be handled, respond with Alexa.ErrorResponse; ensure properties are retrievable and proactivelyReported; user verification may be required for certain directives.

api_knowledge.functionality: Enables devices to control and adjust their brightness levels via Alexa directives and report state changes back to Alexa.
api_knowledge.device_context: Smart home devices that support brightness control, such as light bulbs and dimmers.

use Alexa.PowerLevelController if controlling the power level of an endpoint such as a dimmer switch
implement to let Alexa know the health of your device
use standard discovery mechanism to describe endpoints that support Alexa.BrightnessController
can be reported together with brightness in the same endpoint discovery response

design_constraints: SetBrightness and AdjustBrightness payload must include required properties

api_knowledge.notes_for_root_cause_mapping: If a directive cannot be handled successfully, respond with Alexa.ErrorResponse. Ensure retrievable properties are correctly reported and proactivelyReported properties are updated.

mechanism_feedback.revision: After a power interruption, bulbs may fail to restore or re-establish stored connectivity and operational state, causing them to fail to rejoin the app or recover prior settings.
mechanism_feedback.validation_note: Power-cycle affected and unaffected bulbs while recording persistent configuration, network credentials or pairing state, reconnect attempts, app membership, and restored operational settings; compare whether credentials and settings remain stored but reconnection fails versus whether configuration is actually lost; inspect boot and reconnect logs to distinguish storage-persistence failure from network, hub, cloud, or session-restoration failure.

mechanism_feedback.revision: WiFi setup failures may result from onboarding logic that does not robustly handle some home-network compatibility or provisioning conditions, preventing successful network configuration.
mechanism_feedback.validation_note: Reproduce onboarding across 2.4-GHz-only, 5-GHz-only, dual-band or band-steering, mesh, different authentication modes, and captive-portal or otherwise restricted networks where relevant; capture association, authentication, provisioning, discovery, and app-side error logs; compare failure rates and failure stages across configurations to identify which network conditions actually explain the observed WiFi setup failures.

mechanism_feedback.revision: Mechanical stress at the weak pole-base interface can cause the connection to break or physically disconnect under leverage.
mechanism_feedback.validation_note: Apply controlled bending and leverage loads to the pole-base interface and record displacement, load-to-failure, fracture or separation location, and electrical continuity; inspect failed samples and field returns to determine whether the observed breakage results from connector separation, structural material failure, fastening geometry, solder-joint failure, or internal wiring damage, and compare failure thresholds with expected installation and adjustment loads.

claims.statement: Bulbs frequently fail to rejoin the app or retain settings after a power interruption, indicating instability in state persistence.
Users report connection failures even when the light hub is in close proximity, suggesting issues with local network or protocol handshake.
Setup often fails to connect to WiFi, and retrofitting is sometimes required to enable smart functionality, pointing to onboarding friction.
Physical pole-base connections are reported as weak and prone to breakage under leverage, indicating hardware fragility.
